questions.question_text: In the absence of an explicit Partnership Deed, what is the legal rate of interest allowed on a partner's loan to the firm?
questions.answer: B) 6% per annum

questions.question_text: Which of the following items is NOT recorded in the Income and Expenditure Account of a Not-for-Profit Organisation?
options: D) Subscription received for the current year
questions.answer: C) Life membership fees

questions.question_text: When a new partner brings his share of goodwill in cash, the amount is credited to the old partners in which ratio?
questions.answer: C) Sacrificing ratio

questions.question_text: Accumulated profits and reserves appearing in the balance sheet at the time of a partner's retirement are transferred to:
options: B) All partners' capital accounts in their old profit-sharing ratio
C) Remaining partners' capital accounts in their new profit-sharing ratio
D) Retiring partner's capital account only
questions.answer: B) All partners' capital accounts in their old profit-sharing ratio

questions.question_text: On dissolution of a partnership firm, an unrecorded asset taken over by a partner is debited to:
questions.answer: B) Partner's Capital Account

questions.question_text: Under the capitalization of super profit method, goodwill is calculated by:
options: A) Super Profit / Normal Rate of Return x 100
B) Average Profit / Normal Rate of Return x 100
C) Super Profit x Number of years' purchase
D) Average Profit x Number of years' purchase
questions.answer: A) Super Profit / Normal Rate of Return x 100

questions.question_text: At the time of admission of a new partner, if the value of an asset is found to be undervalued, it will be:
options: C) Debited to Old Partners' Capital Accounts
questions.answer: B) Credited to Revaluation Account

questions.question_text: If the firm assumes the responsibility to pay a partner's private liabilities during dissolution, the corresponding entry credits:
questions.answer: C) Partner's Capital Account

questions.question_text: The balance of the 'Share Forfeiture Account' after the reissue of all forfeited shares is transferred to:
questions.answer: B) Capital Reserve

questions.question_text: A specific donation received by a club for the construction of a pavilion should be shown in:
options: A) Income and Expenditure Account on the income side
B) Income and Expenditure Account on the expenditure side
C) Balance Sheet on the liabilities side
D) Balance Sheet on the assets side
questions.answer: C) Balance Sheet on the liabilities side

questions.question_text: X and Y are partners sharing profits in the ratio of 3:2. Z is admitted for a 1/5th share. What is the new profit-sharing ratio if Z acquires his share entirely from X?
Interest on a partner's drawings is considered as:
options: A) An expense for the firm
B) An income for the firm
C) A liability for the firm
D) An asset for the firm
questions.answer: B) An income for the firm

questions.question_text: The Receipts and Payments Account is a summary of:
questions.answer: B) Cash and bank transactions

questions.question_text: Upon the death of a partner, their share of profit from the beginning of the financial year to the date of death is transferred to:
options: A) Profit and Loss Appropriation Account
B) Profit and Loss Suspense Account
questions.answer: B) Profit and Loss Suspense Account

questions.question_text: Which account is prepared to record the sale of assets and payment of liabilities at the time of firm dissolution?
questions.answer: C) Realisation Account

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): Goodwill is a fictitious asset.
Reason (R): Goodwill has no physical existence but has realizable value.
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
B) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
C) A is true but R is false
D) A is false but R is true
questions.answer: D) A is false but R is true

questions.question_text:
Assertion (A): Rent paid to a partner is a charge against profit.
Reason (R): It is payable even if the firm incurs a loss.
options: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
B) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
C) A is true but R is false
D) A is false but R is true
questions.answer: A) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

questions.question_text: If the firm's total capital is Rs 5,00,000 and the new partner brings Rs 1,50,000 for a 1/4th share, what is the firm's hidden goodwill?
Which of the following is transferred to the Realisation Account at their book value?
options: B) Debit balance of P&L A/c
questions.answer: C) Sundry Debtors

questions.question_text: What is the maximum amount of discount that can be allowed on the reissue of forfeited shares?
options: B) Amount originally received on forfeited shares
C) Amount originally not paid on forfeited shares
questions.answer: B) Amount originally received on forfeited shares

questions.question_text: Define the accounting term 'Sacrificing Ratio' and state when it is calculated during partnership operations. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Sacrificing Ratio is the ratio in which old partners surrender a portion of their profit share in favor of a new partner. It is calculated at the time of admission: Sacrificing Ratio = Old Ratio - New Ratio.

questions.question_text: State the primary difference between a 'Receipts and Payments Account' and an 'Income and Expenditure Account' regarding the basis of accounting. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The Receipts and Payments Account is prepared on a cash basis, recording all cash flows regardless of the period. The Income and Expenditure Account is prepared on an accrual basis, recording revenue items only for the current year.

questions.question_text: Under what condition is 'Interest on Capital' allowed to partners even if it results in a net loss for the firm? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Interest on capital is allowed even in the event of a net loss only when the partnership deed explicitly states that interest on capital is to be treated as a 'charge against profit' rather than an appropriation.

questions.question_text: What is the accounting treatment for unrecorded liabilities discovered during the dissolution of a partnership firm? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Unrecorded liabilities paid during dissolution are directly debited to the Realisation Account and credited to the Cash or Bank Account. They are not transferred to the Realisation Account first since they do not appear in the balance sheet.

questions.question_text: A and B are partners sharing profits in the ratio of 3:2. C is admitted for a 1/4th share in profits. C brings Rs 40,000 as capital and Rs 15,000 as premium for goodwill in cash. Pass the necessary journal entries in the books of the firm. [30-40 words]
questions.answer:
1. Cash A/c Dr 55,000; To C's Capital A/c 40,000; To Premium for Goodwill A/c 15,000. 
2. Premium for Goodwill A/c Dr 15,000; To A's Capital A/c 9,000; To B's Capital A/c 6,000 (Distributed in sacrificing ratio 3:2).

questions.question_text: A partnership firm earned average profits of Rs 80,000 over the last 5 years. The capital employed in the business is Rs 5,00,000 and the normal rate of return is 10%. Calculate the value of goodwill based on 3 years' purchase of super profit. [30-40 words]
questions.answer:
Normal Profit $= 10\%$ of $5,00,000 = 50,000$. 
Super Profit $= Average Profit - Normal Profit = 80,000 - 50,000 = 30,000$. 
Goodwill $= Super Profit \times 3 = 30,000 \times 3 = Rs 90,000$.

questions.question_text: During the dissolution of a firm, sundry creditors amounted to Rs 60,000. Half of the creditors accepted stock worth Rs 28,000 in full settlement of their claim. The remaining creditors were paid at a discount of 10%. Pass the necessary journal entry for the payment to creditors. [30-40 words]
questions.answer:
No entry is passed for the creditors taking over the stock. The remaining creditors (Rs 30,000) are paid at a 10% discount, i.e., Rs 27,000. 
Entry: Realisation A/c Dr 27,000; To Bank A/c 27,000 (Payment made to remaining creditors).

questions.question_text: A sports club received Rs 1,50,000 as subscriptions during the year ending 31st March 2023. Subscriptions outstanding on 31st March 2022 were Rs 10,000 and on 31st March 2023 were Rs 15,000. Subscriptions received in advance on 31st March 2022 were Rs 5,000. Calculate the subscription income to be credited to the Income and Expenditure Account. [30-40 words]
questions.answer:
Subscription received: Rs 1,50,000. 
Less: Outstanding at beginning (Rs 10,000). 
Add: Outstanding at end Rs 15,000. 
Add: Advance at beginning Rs 5,000. 
Income $= 1,50,000 - 10,000 + 15,000 + 5,000 = Rs 1,60,000$ credited to I&E A/c.

questions.question_text: P, Q, and R are partners in a firm. Q retires. His capital account after all adjustments shows a balance of Rs 1,20,000. He is paid Rs 30,000 immediately in cash, and the balance is transferred to his loan account bearing 9% p.a. interest. Pass the necessary journal entry. [30-40 words]
questions.answer:
Q's Capital A/c Dr 1,20,000 
 To Bank A/c 30,000 
 To Q's Loan A/c 90,000 
(Amount due to retiring partner settled by partial cash payment and transferring the balance to his loan account).

questions.question_text: A manager is entitled to a commission of 10% on the net profit after charging such commission. The net profit before charging this commission is Rs 1,10,000. Calculate the manager's commission and the divisible profit. [30-40 words]
questions.answer:
Manager's Commission $= Net Profit \times \frac{Rate}{100 + Rate}$. 
Commission $= 1,10,000 \times \frac{10}{110} = Rs 10,000$. 
Divisible Profit $= Net Profit before commission - Commission = 1,10,000 - 10,000 = Rs 1,00,000$.

sections.section_name: Section D - Long Answer (LA) / Problem Solving

questions.question_text: X and Y are partners sharing profits in the ratio 3:2. Their Balance Sheet as of 31st March 2023 showed creditors Rs 40,000, General Reserve Rs 30,000, and Capitals: X Rs 80,000, Y Rs 60,000. Assets included Cash Rs 20,000, Debtors Rs 50,000, Stock Rs 40,000, and Machinery Rs 1,00,000. Z is admitted for a 1/5 share. Z brings Rs 50,000 as capital. Machinery is undervalued by Rs 10,000 and Stock is overvalued by Rs 5,000. Pass necessary journal entries for Revaluation and General Reserve. [50-60 words]
questions.answer:
1. Machinery A/c Dr 10,000; To Revaluation A/c 10,000. 
2. Revaluation A/c Dr 5,000; To Stock A/c 5,000. 
3. Revaluation A/c Dr 5,000; To X's Cap 3,000; To Y's Cap 2,000 (Revaluation Profit). 
4. General Reserve A/c Dr 30,000; To X's Cap 18,000; To Y's Cap 12,000.

questions.question_text: A, B, and C are partners sharing profits in the ratio of 5:3:2. B retires on 31st March 2023. On that date, the firm's goodwill is valued at Rs 60,000. A and C decide to share future profits in the ratio of 3:2. B's capital after all adjustments regarding reserves and revaluation stands at Rs 90,000. Pass the adjusting entry for goodwill and calculate the final amount payable to B. [50-60 words]
questions.answer:
B's share of goodwill $= 60,000 \times 3/10 = 18,000$. 
Gaining Ratio: A's gain $= 3/5 - 5/10 = 1/10$; C's gain $= 2/5 - 2/10 = 2/10$. Gaining ratio is 1:2. 
Entry: A's Cap A/c Dr 6,000; C's Cap A/c Dr 12,000; To B's Cap A/c 18,000. 
Final amount payable to B $= 90,000 + 18,000 = Rs 1,08,000$.

questions.question_text: The firm of L, M, and N was dissolved on 31st March. Assets realized Rs 1,20,000 against a book value of Rs 1,50,000. Creditors of Rs 40,000 were paid Rs 38,000. Realisation expenses of Rs 2,000 were paid by partner L on behalf of the firm. Unrecorded liability of Rs 5,000 was settled in full. Pass the journal entries for the realization of assets, payment of liabilities, and realization expenses. [50-60 words]
questions.answer:
1. Bank A/c Dr 1,20,000; To Realisation A/c 1,20,000 (Assets realized). 
2. Realisation A/c Dr 38,000; To Bank A/c 38,000 (Creditors paid). 
3. Realisation A/c Dr 2,000; To L's Capital A/c 2,000 (Expenses paid by partner). 
4. Realisation A/c Dr 5,000; To Bank A/c 5,000 (Unrecorded liability paid).

questions.question_text: From the following receipts and payments of a charitable hospital, prepare an Income and Expenditure A/c for the year ended 31st March: Receipts - Subscriptions Rs 80,000, Donations for Building Rs 50,000, Entrance fees Rs 10,000. Payments - Salaries Rs 40,000, Medicines consumed Rs 20,000, Equipment purchased Rs 30,000. Adjustments: Outstanding subscriptions Rs 5,000, Outstanding salaries Rs 4,000. Depreciate equipment by 10%. [50-60 words]
questions.answer:
Income Side: Subscriptions (80k + 5k) = 85,000; Entrance fees = 10,000. Total Income = Rs 95,000. (Building donation is capitalized). 
Expenditure Side: Salaries (40k + 4k) = 44,000; Medicines = 20,000; Depreciation on Equipment = 3,000. Total Expenditure = Rs 67,000. 
Surplus = 95,000 - 67,000 = Rs 28,000.
